interface.signature: n: int, leftChild: List[int], rightChild: List[int] -> bool

preconditions.expression: n >= 1 and n <= 10**4 and len(leftChild) == n and len(rightChild) == n
preconditions.description: n is a positive integer within bounds, and leftChild/rightChild lists match n in length.

preconditions.expression: all(-1 <= child <= n - 1 for child in leftChild + rightChild)
preconditions.description: Every child index in leftChild and rightChild is either -1 (no child) or a valid node index in [0, n-1].

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= i < n for i in range(n)) and any(i == 0 for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The nodes are numbered from 0 to n-1, and node 0 exists as the root candidate.

postconditions.expression: len({i for i in range(n) if i not in leftChild and i not in rightChild}) == 1
postconditions.description: Exactly one node (the root) has no parent (i.e., does not appear in leftChild or rightChild).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= leftChild[i] < n and 0 <= rightChild[i] < n for i in range(n) if leftChild[i] != -1 and rightChild[i] != -1)
postconditions.description: All non-null child indices are valid node indices in [0, n-1].

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= parent < n for parent in range(n) if (leftChild[parent] == i or rightChild[parent] == i) for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: Every node (except root) has exactly one parent (appears exactly once in leftChild or rightChild).

postconditions.expression: not any(i in leftChild and i in rightChild for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: No node appears as both a left and right child of any parent (no duplicate children).

postconditions.expression: return_value == (all(0 <= leftChild[i] < n and 0 <= rightChild[i] < n for i in range(n) if leftChild[i] != -1 and rightChild[i] != -1) and len({i for i in range(n) if i not in leftChild and i not in rightChild}) == 1 and all(0 <= parent < n for parent in range(n) if (leftChild[parent] == i or rightChild[parent] == i) for i in range(n)) and not any(i in leftChild and i in rightChild for i in range(n)))
postconditions.description: The function returns true if and only if the nodes form exactly one valid binary tree: exactly one root, no cycles, no duplicate children, and all child indices are valid.
